bounded_statement: In this case only, the workflow assigns the sorter's discrete predicted level labels (values confined to the finite set {0,1,2}) to the exposure position of the association model, whereas the governing task authorizes only the continuous expected level index computed from the sorter's per-level shares; the reported coefficient -5.753846 is therefore produced from the disallowed discrete level assignment rather than the authorized continuous exposure.

counterevidence_considered.description: The authorized continuous quantity is actually computed in the workflow (the probability-weighted expected level index), which could suggest compliance; however, it is aliased to `plain` and never assigned to `exposure`, so it does not reach the association model.

evidence.description: The task mandates that the exposure be the expected value of the ordered level index under the sorter's per-level shares, kept continuous, and explicitly disqualifies any quantity confined to the finite set of level values.

source_refs.quoted_text: Apply the named workflow to the complete staged row sequence. The quantity that enters the association model's exposure position must be the expected value of the ordered level index under the sorter's own per-level shares, kept on its continuous scale. A quantity confined to the finite set of level values does not satisfy this task.

evidence.description: The workflow computes the discrete predicted label and assigns it to the exposure position; `sorter.predict` on a LogisticRegression fitted to integer levels {0,1,2} returns only values from that finite set.
The exposure feeds directly into the association model whose single coefficient is the reported result, so the report's value is a function of the discrete label exposure.

extensions.x-stage1-falsification-attempt: I tried to falsify by checking (a) whether `label` could coincide with the continuous expectation: it cannot, because `predict` returns the argmax class from {0,1,2} while `mean` is a probability-weighted average that is generically non-integer, so the two quantities differ in kind exactly as the task's exclusion clause describes; (b) whether `exposure = label` could be dead code: it is not, since `exposure` is the sole regressor in the summary fit whose coefficient is written to the report; (c) whether the report might have been produced by a different exposure than the code shows: the visible files give no indication of any other producer of results/report.md. No falsification succeeded.

root_cause: The line `exposure = label` routes `sorter.predict(features)` (a finite-set level assignment) into the association regression instead of `mean = shares @ np.array([0.0, 1.0, 2.0])`, which is the continuous quantity the task explicitly authorizes and which the workflow computes but never uses as exposure.
